sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage; company law codified in the Law of 10 August 1915; commercial law in the Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Governments of Belgium and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 6 June 2005; in force 1 December 2009), replacing the 1984 China-BLEU BIT

Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (in force)

Convention between the United States of America and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (in force since 20 December 2000)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49 and 63 (freedom of establishment; free movement of capital)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI), in force for Luxembourg since 1 July 2019

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme (AML/CFT Law, as amended, including the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) (Luxembourg UBO register; restrictive access confirmed after CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20, which precludes general public access); Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS); CSSF rules and FATF 40 Recommendations applied as professional reference standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and articles of association (statuts) to be executed before a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial deed executed in Luxembourg (no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation (procuration) granted by non-resident corporate shareholder to the Luxembourg notary or local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if HCCH 1961 party state) OR Consular Legalization via Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence / extract from the foreign trade register (for any non-resident corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade registry of the shareholder's state of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing issued for the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or authorized registered agent of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Copies of passports of ultimate beneficial owners and appointed managers (gérants)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority or certified copy by local notary or consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for certified copies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing credit institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document retained in AML file (no apostille required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, managers (gérants), and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the US OFAC SDN list, the UK HMT sanctions list (where applicable), and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance / CSSF frozen-assets directives. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any PEP status, high-risk third-country nexus, or opaque nominee structure, in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and Article 3 of the Law of 12 November 2004. AML/CFT records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship under Article 4-2 of the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online platform at www.lbr.lu, operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed using Latin-script characters; French, German, and Luxembourgish are the accepted administrative languages of the RCS. A non-Latin trade name (e.g., Chinese characters) for the B2B marketplace store must be transliterated into Latin characters and is registered in that transliteration. The name must be distinctive, truthful, non-misleading, and distinguishable from all existing RCS entries, per Article 2 of the Law of 10 August 1915 and the RCS Law of 19 December 2002.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank / banque / bancaire (requires CSSF banking authorization)
insurance / assurance / assurances (requires CAA insurance authorization)
investment fund / fonds d'investissement / FCP / SICAV (requires CSSF fund authorization)
securities exchange / bourse de valeurs / stock exchange (requires financial regulator clearance)
S.A. / S.A.R.L. / S.C.A. / S.C.S. (misleading corporate-form suffixes unless corresponding exactly to the statutory form)
Luxembourg / Lëtzebuerg / state emblem or coat of arms (implying false state sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant or the instructing Luxembourg notary receives the stated grounds for refusal. The applicant may (1) submit a revised name application through the LBR online portal; (2) request a written RCS rejection confirmation; (3) lodge an administrative appeal (recours) before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (administrative chamber) within three months of notification; (4) pursue further judicial review before the Cour d'appel. There is no statutory extension of the initial 30-day name clearance validity; a fresh availability search and reservation cycle must be initiated upon expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible at incorporation only through a licensed domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation) regulated by the Law of 31 May 1999. For this B2B cross-border platform, a pure virtual office without local management presence, premises, and administrative substance creates material tax-residence, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse risks under Luxembourg and OECD BEPS standards. A full-service domiciliation with dedicated administrative substance in Luxembourg is the recommended minimum; a physical office should be secured once operational revenue materializes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 20% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months and approximately 35% within 36 months for a Standard-Risk B2B platform operating through a licensed domiciliation agent; probability rises to approximately 60% where VAT registration, cross-border logistics, or unusual transaction patterns trigger review by the Luxembourg tax administration or the police financial crime unit (BLCR).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS search fee per current LBR tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial emoluments scale under the Grand-Ducal decree on notarial tariffs; inclusive of disbursements and deed copies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing (dépôt au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR deposit fee for a commercial company filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Government of Luxembourg – Official Gazette (Journal officiel / RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of the official gazette

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, good standing, power of attorney, passports; approximate 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (apostille authority) of the foreign jurisdiction and/or Luxembourg consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention per-document tariff (approx. 25-60 USD per document) plus consular statutory fees for non-HCCH jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / licensed domiciliation package (first-year pro-rata at incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RBE filing is free of charge; professional compliance due-diligence fee benchmark of EUR 400 - 600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate documents into French, German, or English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page tariff benchmark of EUR 35 - 55 per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence retainer of Luxembourg regulatory counsel (B2B marketplace licensing review and cross-border platform structuring)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm admitted to the Luxembourg Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark hourly rate of EUR 250 - 450 per hour; fixed retainer for Stage 1 scope

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank / payments institution KYC file preparation for future corporate account and SWIFT Wire / Alibaba_Pay payment rails connectivity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate bank or licensed electronic money institution relationship desk / fintech onboarding agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for corporate KYC and onboarding package (not a regulatory filing fee)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated, Articles 710-1 et seq. (Société à responsabilité limitée/S.à r.l.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Code of Civil Procedure provisions on electronic filing and publication in RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), acting for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg District Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized acte constitutif (articles of association / incorporation deed), filed electronically with the RCS for legal effectiveness and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et des associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000 for an S.à r.l., fully subscribed and fully paid up upon incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked bank account in the name of the company in formation (or notary escrow) and remain blocked until RCS registration evidence is provided. In-kind contributions require compliance with asset valuation rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the articles of association and all ancillary incorporation documents submitted to the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register be, and are hereby, approved, and that each subscriber's share subscription be, and is hereby, ratified, in accordance with the share capital table annexed. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office of the Company be established at [Registered Office], Luxembourg, and the Manager be instructed to execute lease and administrative formalities. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Manager Name] be, and is hereby, appointed as Manager (Gérant) of the Company, with full powers to manage, sign, open bank accounts, receive share capital releases, and complete all filings required for legal operation, until removed by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary, with name verification through the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed corporate name for identity or confusing similarity in the RCS. Prepare final articles of association (statuts), preferably in French or German. All incorporators or duly authorized proxies must appear before the Luxembourg notary. The notary authenticates the acte constitutif, collects the data required for RCS filing, and coordinates publication in RESA.
required_dossiers: RCS name search or name reservation confirmation
Valid passports or national identity cards of all shareholders and managers
Bank certificate of blocked funds or notary escrow receipt
Written powers of attorney for any proxy signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects to the name or the articles, obtain written reasons, amend the text via supplementary notarized deed, and refile. Minor formatting/translation defects are cured by the notary without repeat notarization where law permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Share Capital Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary escrow account, such as Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) or a regulated commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the S.à r.l. 'en formation' or a notary escrow account. Deposit the full minimum share capital of EUR 12,000. Obtain a formal bank blocking certificate confirming full payment and unencumbered availability. Capital is released only after RCS registration is made public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account or releases funds early, request corrective blocking documentation or transfer the contribution to another Luxembourg financial institution. If source-of-funds documents are requested, provide audited statements or transaction evidence within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the acte constitutif, blocking certificate, registered office details, and officer appointment through the LBR electronic filing system. Pay the required official RCS and RESA publication fees. Upon registration, the company obtains its RCS registration number and the incorporation extract is published in the RESA electronic publication.
required_dossiers: Registered office evidence or lease commitment
Fee payment confirmation from the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the notary must submit a supplementary explanation or rectifying deed. Substantive corrections require a new shareholder resolution and additional RESA publication. Appeals against refusal may be lodged with the District Court of Luxembourg within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security and Occupational Health and Safety Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the CCSS for employee/manager social security coverage within the statutory delay from commencement of activity. Submit the employer declaration, manager self-employed status where applicable, and any employee records. Notify the ITM of the business premises for occupational safety registration if physical premises are used.
required_dossiers: Occupational health and safety self-declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS identifies a lapse in declaration, submit the missing employer registration and contribution statement promptly. Late-registration penalties may be reduced upon showing good cause. ITM inspections are curable by immediate adoption of safety protocols.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Electronic Marketplace Formal Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Ministry of the Economy for informational classification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete corporate income tax registration with the ACD and, where relevant, register for Luxembourg value added tax (VAT) with the AEDT. For the B2B wholesale marketplace model, confirm the absence of any sectoral industrial licence. Maintain transaction-flow documentation for cross-border payment rails such as Alibaba_Pay and SWIFT Wire.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and articles of association
Residence certificate for the registered office
Bank account details including BIC/SWIFT and IBAN
Completed standard CLN/CN registration forms of the ACD
Description of platform services and supply-chain flows for VAT classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Tax registration queries are cured by filing a formal response and supporting article of association within the prescribed ACD/AEDT timeframe. If VAT status is disputed, submit a reasoned position under the VAT Directive and Luxembourg VAT law; default registration may be withdrawn by appeal within the statutory 30-day period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 B2B electronic wholesale platform operation; if physical premises are established, the competent authority is the Ministry of the Economy and, where a regulated establishment permit applies, the competent district inspectorate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operational or manufacturing permit is required for a purely electronic B2B marketplace platform. The company operates under ordinary RCS registration and general e-commerce/consumer-protection law; physical office use requires only a standard commercial occupancy authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/none required. The B2B electronic marketplace platform involves no industrial installations, no production process, and no discharge-generating activity, and therefore no environmental impact assessment or environmental operating permit is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated from the electronic platform operations. Waste handling, if any, must comply with the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; any later warehousing or logistics activity would require assessment under the threshold decrees of the Luxembourg environmental law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the physical registered office, the company must obtain an occupancy or building-safety confirmation from the competent municipal commune, including compliance with public fire-safety and structural load standards. Workplace clearance requires registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and adherence to the Law of 17 June 1994 on occupational safety and health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue – Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/registration duties; official e-portal: myguichet.lu (business e-filing via MyGuichet / eTVA module); e-VAT filing at aedt.public.lu.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting together with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. There is no foreign exchange control legislation, no prior central bank authorisation for foreign exchange transactions, and no restriction on the free movement of capital and payments between EU member states and third countries, subject only to EU sanctions, anti-money laundering rules, and statistical reporting obligations. Profit remittances are unrestricted from an exchange control perspective; however, any dividend distribution must satisfy Luxembourg corporate law solvency tests and may be subject to domestic dividend withholding tax unless exempted under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules in Luxembourg. Exporters are not required to convert, repatriate, or sell foreign currency earnings. Export receipts may be retained in any currency, settled in EUR, or used for commercial hedging. The only obligation is the bank's and direct respondent's duty to report cross-border transactions above the applicable BCL threshold (generally EUR 12,500 per transaction) for balance of payments statistics.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dedicated capital contribution escrow account and operational multi-currency current account
Corporate operating current account with segregated capital escrow sub-account
Operational current account and capital injection escrow account
Corporate current account and trade-finance facility account
EUR operational account and multi-currency settlement account
Wholesale operational account for cross-border treasury, escrow for capital subscription

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium-to-High only if the EMI is licensed in Luxembourg or validly passporting under PSD2 within the EEA. Offshore digital EMIs outside the EEA cannot provide payment services to a Luxembourg SARL without a local establishment or a licensed Luxembourg agent. Using an offshore or non-regulated EMI as the primary payment rail is legally incompatible with the CSSF framework and will create substantive AML/KYC blockers at any tier-1 Luxembourg bank. Recommended practice: route platform payouts through a CSSF-regulated payment institution or an EEA-passported EMI, while maintaining a direct SWIFT/Mainland account at a Luxembourg credit institution for core treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require physical presence for at least one statutory manager or authorised signatory of the SARL at account opening for a corporate entity, particularly when non-EU shareholders or complex cross-border structures are involved. Remote video identification is legally possible for natural persons under CSSF Circular 17/655, but most commercial banks restrict its use and often require an in-person interview for e-commerce or marketplace clients. For a B2B cross-border platform SARL, the decisive KYC interview will ordinarily take place at the bank's Luxembourg office, with certified copies, apostilled corporate documents, and original board resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners domiciled in a high-risk or non-transparent jurisdiction, or complex multi-layered ownership chain involving overseas holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS Luxembourg commercial register extract (less than 3 months old); official Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) extract; full legal ownership chart identifying all 25% or greater shareholders; notarised power of attorney and board resolution; passport copies and proof of address for all UBOs; sanctions and PEP screening reports; sworn statement of source of wealth; professional bank reference letters from the UBO's relationship bank; tax identification numbers of UBOs; apostilled or legalised corporate registration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Luxembourg economic substance, perceived shell risk, or tax-residency ambiguity of the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease for registered office in Luxembourg; staffing evidence such as payroll records, local administration contracts, and authorised local office manager; business plan detailing treasury, procurement, marketing, and support functions performed in Luxembourg; audited or reviewed financial statements; annual board minutes and management decision logs; evidence of annual accounts filings at the RCS; Luxembourg income tax residency certificate obtained from the Luxembourg direct tax administration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-transaction-volume B2B marketplace revenue received through third-party payment processors, with risk of commingled funds or opaque settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform agreement and settlement service contract tracing funds from Alibaba Pay or equivalent processor to the SARL's bank account; detailed reconciliation of gross collections, commissions, refunds, and net payouts; underlying trade invoice package (purchase orders, VAT invoices, packing lists, bills of lading); e-commerce dashboard access or attested monthly reports; internal AML/CTF procedure manual with transaction monitoring and red-flag filters; external audit certificate relating to fund flows; privacy and GDPR compliance documentation; contractual framework with both buyers and sellers NFT? (within scope); historical bank statements from previous payment processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained inconsistencies between stated turnover, transaction narrative, and the account activity profile, or heavy dependence on high-risk correspondent corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified accounts receivable and payable ledger; invoices and contracts covering at least 12 months of projected operations; customs and EORI-related trade documentation if goods are imported or exported; a letter of explanation from the chairman or manager; statutory audited financial statements once available; supplier and buyer due diligence files; corporate AML policy; transaction flow maps for inbound and outbound money movement; affirmation from a licensed Luxembourg external accountant (CAC) or certified auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholders' equity contributions must be credited in EUR to the SARL's dedicated capital contribution escrow account at a Luxembourg bank. The credit transfer shall be initiated by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account, with the reference text stating 'SHARE CAPITAL INCREASE / RESERVE / APIC' and identifying the contributing shareholder. For cross-border operations equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500, the BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation arises and is generally discharged by the receiving bank on behalf of the client. The bank will verify the notarised share subscription document, the board resolution authorising the capital increase, the RCS filing confirmation and the investment/service agreement. After the funds are credited and compliance checks are completed, the capital increase is notarised and filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound settlement rely primarily on SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to overseas trade suppliers, using TARGET2 for intra-EUR transactions and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for urgent low-value settlements. For larger cross-border purchases requiring documentary security, an irrevocable at-sight commercial letter of credit issued by a Luxembourg bank and advised through a correspondent bank is the appropriate instrument. Standby letters of credit may be used as performance guarantees. Non-EUR and EUR treasury payments will be executed through the bank's nostro accounts; every outgoing transaction must be backed by an underlying trade document in the bank's client file. All transactions above the BCL threshold must be captured in the monthly balance of payments report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in major convertible currencies, entered into with an authorised Luxembourg bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies lacking an active deliverable market, only where a genuine underlying commercial exposure exists
European-style FX options for revenue and payment protection
FX swaps to manage temporary liquidity mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps qualifying under EMIR clearing or bilateral margin rules
Spot FX buys for immediate settlement of commercial obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders approving the annual accounts and granting discharge to management (approbation des comptes annuels et quitus)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body; minutes recorded in the statutory minute book; no government filing at this step
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers' civil liability to the company and third parties; any shareholder may petition the District Court to convene the meeting; audit opinion may be qualified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, management report and, if applicable, statutory auditor's report) with the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end (by 31 July for a 31 December year-end); e-filing mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 100-EUR 5,000; repeated non-filing exposes the company to court-ordered strike-off (radiation d'office) and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual tax return for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March following the tax year; automatic extension to 31 December when prepared and filed by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, late-filing surcharge, tax assessment by estimation, and fines up to EUR 25,000 under the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax (impôt minimum sur la fortune) settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: EUR 1,500 or EUR 3,500 flat annual minimum depending on total balance sheet; reported in the annual IFT return due by 31 December at the latest (calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Enforced tax collection, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, and loss of the right to carry forward tax losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-ownership record (RBE) update and annual consistency verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) - Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Amendment filing within one month of any change in direct or indirect shareholding or control; documented internal annual verification by 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines and possible imprisonment for repeat non-compliance; banks and payment institutions may decline or terminate the business relationship.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises is mandatory when the SARL exceeds two of three criteria at year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4,400,000; net turnover > EUR 8,800,000; average workforce > 50 FTE. Small undertakings below these thresholds are exempt from the audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts of undertakings (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is optional and was not selected for this SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg imposes no separate annual UBO re-declaration; the RBE entry must be amended within one month of any beneficial-ownership change under the Law of 13 January 2019. Perform a documented annual reconciliation at the AGM date among the Register of Members, notarial or written share-transfer deeds, and the RBE platform, with sign-off recorded in the minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des associés and parts sociales, including share transfers)
Register of Directors and Managers (gérants and directors)
Minute Book of shareholders' and management meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 5,000 per annum (EUR 1,600 - EUR 4,400), covering registered office, domiciliation, corporate secretarial support and RCS filing assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 - USD 28,000 per audit year (EUR 8,000 - EUR 25,000) when the statutory audit is mandatory; not required for a small SARL below the size thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC) + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19% effective national rate; aggregate with Luxembourg City municipal business tax (6.75%) = 24.94% (commune-dependent)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains from ≥10% or ≥€1.2M participations held ≥12 months); IP box (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, ~5% effective rate); notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity; double deduction/incentives not available for non-resident-deemed activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via the eCDF portal of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD); ancillary schedules for the impôt commercial communal and impôt sur la fortune
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g. FY ending 31 December 2024 is due by 31 December 2025); must be filed by the SARL's legal representative or accredited tax agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, registered office, national identification number (NIF), RCSL trade-register number, eCDF filing code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the SARL's Luxembourg NIF and RCSL number only; non-resident shareholders are not identified on the return caption except in the shareholder schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B - Fiscal year and tax status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year; indicator that the SARL is fully subject to Luxembourg CIT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg SARL is always resident; non-resident management does not alter the entity's residency or the head-line filing obligations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit/loss of the B2B marketplace (audited P&L basis ISIC 4791; NAICS 425120)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross receipts from platform commissions and cross-border settlement fees; enter the result before any tax adjustments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reintegration of non-deductible expenses: unsupported management fees, unconfirmed provisions, penalties, 50% of certain representation costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-arm's-length service fees paid to non-resident related parties must be added back unless supported by a transfer pricing study

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of participation-exempt dividends, exempt capital gains, IP-box exempt portion (80%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the shareholder register and evidence of 12-month holding; no exemption where the parent is resident in a zero-tax jurisdiction and lacks substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year losses against current taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-recognized assessed losses qualify; no surrender of losses from foreign group companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after adjustments, exemptions and loss offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base for applying 17% CIT; recomputation required if ACD rejects TP adjustments or exemption claims

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre I - Tax computation and municipal tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT at 17%; solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT; municipal business tax at the commune rate (e.g. 6.75% Luxembourg City)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot offset their home-state taxes on this line; foreign tax credits are only recognized at Cadre J

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre J - Tax credits and NID
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit for underlying WHT/TT on foreign-source income; notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty credits only on the STRICTLY foreign-source part of the taxable base and attach supporting TRCs

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax due or refundable after prepayments (acomptes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by separate order to the ACD bank account; non-resident intermediaries cannot settle the SARL's CIT

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine (generally €100–€12,000 per return, escalating for repeat offenders) plus a 10% late-payment surcharge and default interest of 9% per annum on the unpaid tax; non-filing after formal demand may trigger net-worth assessment (taxation d'office) and criminal exposure

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory; fully eliminated (0%) for qualifying EU parent-subsidiary / participation-exemption distributions (≥10% or acquisition value ≥€1.2M held ≥12 months, substance and anti-abuse satisfied); treaty rates typically 5% for ≥10% investors and 10–15% for portfolio holdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: obtain an annual Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax authority. Step 2: lodge the TRC with a Luxembourg dividend-relief claim form to the ACD (or the paying company for at-source reduction) before or at the payment date. Step 3: where the 15% has been withheld, file a refund application with the ACD within the standard 5-year limitation window; attach evidence of beneficial ownership, share register and holding-period proof. Step 4: satisfy the anti-abuse/substance test (no conduit arrangement, real activity of the parent).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic WHT on IP royalties paid to non-residents (treaty-protected; no Luxembourg WHT imposed at source). Interest: 0% WHT on ordinary cross-border debt interest; only interest on profit-participating loans may be recharacterized and exposed to the 15% dividend rate by analogy.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue (mandatory CbCR); no fixed domestic statutory threshold for Master/Local File, but ACD may order full TP documentation for any intra-group flow within 15 days, and practical safe compliance starts at EUR 1,000,000 intercompany turnover
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Luxembourg ESR law equivalent to the UAE's Economic Substance Regulations; substance is enforced indirectly through: Article 6 LIR abuse-of-law doctrine, ATAD GAAR, participation-exemption abuse clause, DTA PPT / beneficial-ownership rules, and ACD administrative practice requiring local registered office, local management decisions, employees, own accounting records and local bank accounts for treaty/WHT relief claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of B2B marketplace commissions, fabrication of invoices between the SARL and offshore related parties, concealment of Alibaba-Pay/SWIFT receipts from the ACD
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of evaded CIT plus 10% late-payment surcharge and 9% p.a. default interest; criminal fine between EUR 5,000 and EUR 50,000 (doubled on relapse within 10 years) and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or de facto director is criminally liable as principal; civil recovery via 'action en comblement du passif' against insolvent mismanagement; courts may impose passport seizure, travel ban (interdiction de sortie du territoire) and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / substance abuse and treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mailbox SARL with no office, no employees, no local decisions, used solely to funnel dividends/royalties to a low-tax parent and to claim the 0% WHT or treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of participation exemption and treaty relief; recharacterization of distributions as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT plus interest; retroactive reassessment with 10% surcharge; publication of the decision and potential CFC/inclusion adjustment abroad
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false substance declarations or beneficiary-owner forms face abuse-of-law reassessment exposures, civil liability to the shareholders, and criminal charges for false certification where intent is proven

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing Master/Local File, absent functional analysis for the platform services, non-arm's-length commissions to non-resident related entities, failure to file CbCR for groups above EUR 750M, disregarding ACD information orders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to the arm's-length profit plus correlated secondary adjustments, default interest at 9% p.a. and a 10% surcharge on the deficiency; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for failure to produce documentation, with daily astreinte for continuing non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be ordered to complete the company's loss (comblement du passif) where TP adjustments render the company insolvent; continued non-cooperation subjects management to fines and, in flagrant cases, criminal tax evasion prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / DAC7 platform reporting and payment-rail abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the B2B digital marketplace and report seller data to the ACD under DAC7, absence of KYC/UBO files for Alibaba-Pay and SWIFT counterparties, structuring cross-border payments to avoid thresholds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DAC7 non-reporting penalties up to EUR 20,000 per annual cycle; AML administrative fines for legal persons up to EUR 1,250,000 or three times the illicit benefit; criminal money-laundering exposure up to 5 years' imprisonment for the responsible officers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Luxembourg AML law imposes direct duties on the gérant; failure to file suspicious-transaction reports or to maintain UBO registers exposes the director to personal fines, travel bans, and disqualification; civil compensation to third parties is available under Article 1382 of the Civil Code
